messages.subject: help me, what's wrong?
parts:
Hello,
I'm trying to build an app to do something like that: the user clicks with the mouse on a graphic to create a discrete probability distribution (namely, a load die). I put also a button to reset the die, with uniform probabilities. But after pushing the reset button the chart doesn't show the right distribution: it seems that it "remembers" the last click, and this particular point maintains its last value, while the others are recomputed so that the probabilities sum up to one. Since the other points are equal between them, I can see that a) the reset is working, but b) for some reason the coordinates from the last click are not cleared though that click was already managed, previous to the reset. That doesn't make sense to me!

Of course, I'm still a beginner in the shiny techniques, and the code has to include several errors. I would appreciate very much some advise about the right way to program this app. A simplified version of the program is attached to the topic.

Thank you in advance

JA

messages.subject: Re: help me, what's wrong?
parts:
Hi folks,

I've found a pretty nice solution. I check for both events, the action button and the mouse click.

  v <- reactiveValues(p=array(1/6, dim=6))

  observeEvent(input$reset, {
    v$p <-rep(1/6, 6)
  })
 
  observeEvent(input$P, {
 a = input$P$x
 b = input$P$y
 if (abs(round(a)-a)<0.3 & b>0 & b<1) {
a = round(a)
p = update_p(v$p, b, a)
v$p <- p
 }
  })
  
regards
